agentNetwork.identityHeadersHelp: Pick which wire headers carry the caller's identity on every upstream request. The proxy strips any client-supplied value first, so an app can't spoof identity. Leave a field empty to disable stamping for that dimension. The defaults shown as placeholders use the <dim>x-bf-dim-*</dim> family (Prometheus / OTEL — requires a matching declaration in your gateway's <prometheus>client.prometheus_labels</prometheus> config). Switch to <log>x-bf-lh-*</log> to use Bifrost's always-on log-metadata path instead — no gateway-side config needed there.
agentNetwork.individualCapTooltip: Caps each member's own consumption within the window. A user that hits this cap is blocked even when the group still has headroom.
agentNetwork.jsonMetadataHelp: NetBird stamps a JSON object onto the <header>{header}</header> header with the caller's identity so the gateway's logs and analytics key off the real user, not whichever app process happens to hold the API token. Pick the JSON key names that match your existing log filters; leave a field empty to omit that key from the JSON. The proxy strips any client-supplied value first, so an app can't spoof identity.
agentNetwork.kimiClaudeCodeNote: Pairs with a Kimi provider keeping the default upstream URL <upstream>https://api.moonshot.ai</upstream>. The <suffix>/anthropic</suffix> suffix in the base URL rides through the endpoint to Moonshot, which serves the Anthropic Messages API under that path.

agentNetwork.litellmIdentityMappingsHelp: Groups are written into <tags>metadata.tags</tags> in the JSON body so LiteLLM can enforce tag budgets and rate limits. The user identity is sent in the <userHeader>x-litellm-end-user-id</userHeader> header. The proxy strips any client-supplied value first, so an app can't spoof identity. The configured API key must be a LiteLLM virtual key with <allowTags>metadata.allow_client_tags: true</allowTags>, or LiteLLM silently drops these tags.

agentNetwork.openrouterAttributionHelp: NetBird stamps the caller's user identity onto the request body's <user>user</user> field — that's the OpenAI-standard field OpenRouter consults for per-user analytics. The proxy overwrites any client-supplied value first, so an app can't spoof identity.
agentNetwork.openrouterNoGroups: No groups dimension. OpenRouter does not document a per-request tag, label, or team field — only per-user identity. NetBird's group memberships are not propagated to OpenRouter; if you need per-group attribution, query NetBird's own access log instead of OpenRouter's analytics.

agentNetwork.portkeyMetadataHelp: NetBird stamps the <header>x-portkey-metadata</header> header with a JSON object so Portkey's analytics and budgets key off the real caller. The proxy strips any client-supplied value first, so an app can't spoof identity. Per Portkey's 128-character cap each value is truncated when needed. The mapping is fixed in this release.
agentNetwork.privateClusterRequired: You need a reverse proxy cluster with private capabilities in order to enable agent networks. Connect one under <link>Configuration → Clusters</link> before adding a provider.
agentNetwork.promptCaptureBody: NetBird redacts emails, SSN-shaped, phone-shaped, and credit-card patterns before storing the prompt body. Enabling this guardrail adds strict redaction on top of the proxy's built-in token redaction.

agentNetwork.vercelCaveats: Caveats: Vercel caps tags at 10 per request (each 1–64 chars) and the user value at 256 chars. Members of more than 10 groups will see Vercel reject the request with HTTP 400 — re-scope group memberships if you hit it. Vercel charges $0.075 per 1,000 unique user/tag values written; budget accordingly for high-cardinality use cases.
agentNetwork.vercelIdentityHeadersHelp: NetBird stamps the user identity and group list onto <user>ai-reporting-user</user> and <tags>ai-reporting-tags</tags> on every upstream request. Vercel groups its Custom Reporting API by these dimensions (<byUser>group_by=user</byUser> / <byTag>group_by=tag</byTag>). Header names are fixed by Vercel's API contract — renaming would silently disable attribution. The proxy strips any client-supplied value first.
agentNetwork.virtualApiKeyHelp: The raw virtual key configured for strict API-key authentication on agentgateway.
agentNetwork.virtualKeyTrustNote: The virtual key authenticates NetBird but does not make headers from another network path trustworthy.
